catalogueClaim: none — these pairs are discrimination material for the spend hunt's attackability axis. They add no S00 vector row and assert no defect in any contract they contain.
note: A HOLDOUT is a set the instrument is measured on and was not built from. This namespace is not that yet, and the manifest says so in every row. Each `expectedVerdict` was recorded from the instrument's own output on 2026-09-26, by an author with the instrument in front of them, in the same change. A recorded expectation that reproduces is therefore SELF-CONSISTENCY, not a discovery: the harness reports it under `selfConsistency` and reports the discovery denominator separately. Nothing here is node-validated, nothing is an accepted execution, and no verdict is a property violation. A miss is never safe: `notUnderProbes` and `requiresProof` say only that these probes produced no pass and no residual respectively.

independence.rule: An item may enter the discovery denominator only when its `authoring` is `independent` AND the measured corpus scan finds neither a verbatim file nor a shared clause in the visible corpus. The eligible denominator is DERIVED from those two facts by the harness; this text states the rule and asserts nothing about the outcome.

authoringValues.independent: authored by someone with no access to the instrument's output for this namespace
authoringValues.instrument-visible: authored with the instrument's output in hand — reproduces expectations, earns no discovery credit

caps.selfBoxDefault: none — the instrument's synthetic SELF (no registers, value 0), declared per item where a real box is supplied

pairs.basis: The successor's propositionBytes equality is the only clause the attacker's pay-back sample fails: the pay-back carries SELF's value and tokens under its own script. Deleting it leaves a value floor the sample satisfies, so the pair separates on this instrument and the separation is attributable to the deleted clause.

With the key the record's only evidence is a residual proposition; without it the preserve sample passes. The pair separates, and the difference is the key requirement — not a claim that a keyless preservation step is a defect. Whether it is intended is the author's claim, which this namespace does not make.
pairs.instrumentLimit: The counterexample retains `OUTPUTS.size == 1`, and this instrument cannot see it: every probe builds exactly one output, so the clause is inert under these probes. The harness measures that inertness rather than leaving it as a claim.

pairs.basis: The height bound is the only clause the preserve sample fails: it is beyond every sampled height, so the control's evidence is 'no probe passed and no residual observed'. Deleting it leaves the successor binding, which the preserve sample satisfies. The control's `notUnderProbes` is a statement about these probes, never a safety claim.

The token-amount floor is satisfied by both samples, so the pair separates on the successor's propositionBytes equality and not on the floor: the floor's presence must not hide the separation. A declared self box supplies the token — see `instrumentLimit`.
pairs.instrumentLimit: Both items run against a caller-supplied SELF carrying one token. Under the instrument's synthetic SELF (no tokens) the same counterexample reports `notUnderProbes`, because `tokens(0)` throws. The self box is therefore part of the measurement, not decoration, and is declared per item.

items.expectedBasis: The preserve sample copies SELF's script and value, so the successor's script binding and value floor both hold; the attacker's own script fails the propositionBytes equality. One preserve sample passed and no attacker sample did.

Only the value floor remains, and the attacker's pay-back sample carries SELF's own value, so a probe passed with no proof. SELF is synthetic (no registers, value 0), so the floor is trivially satisfied and this says nothing about a funded box.

The key is required, so no sample passes and the record's evidence is a residual `ProveDlog` proposition. `requiresProof` is neither safe nor vulnerable: it says only that these probes reduced to a proof requirement.
The successor binding alone holds for the preserve sample. The counterexample is the same binding without a key, so the record reports a keyless preservation step and no loss.

The height bound is beyond every sampled height and the successor binding fails the attacker sample, so no probe passed and no residual was observed. This is explicitly not a safety statement: a contract that is unspendable under twelve synthetic samples has not been shown safe.
Without the height bound the successor binding is the whole condition, which the preserve sample satisfies. The transition under test is that the release became unconditional.

With a supplied SELF carrying one token, the successor's token-amount floor holds for the preserve sample (which copies SELF's tokens) and the attacker's own script still fails the propositionBytes equality.

The token-amount floor alone is satisfied by the attacker's pay-back sample, which carries SELF's tokens, so a probe passed with no proof. Under the instrument's synthetic SELF the same contract reports `notUnderProbes` because `tokens(0)` throws — which is why the self box is declared rather than defaulted.
